company.name: InterGlobe Aviation
company.business_summary: India's largest airline with ~60% domestic market share; 350+ aircraft fleet (A320 family); low-cost carrier model; no fuel hedging policy; expanding international routes.

event.headline: Crude oil spikes to $110
key_facts: ATF (Aviation Turbine Fuel) price linked to crude; ~38% of IndiGo costs
IndiGo market share ~60% domestic; fleet 350+ aircraft
No fuel hedging policy (unlike global peers)
unknowns: Fare hike ability in price-sensitive market
Domestic demand resilience at higher fares

channels.reason: ATF ~38% of total costs; directly crude-linked; no hedging
Lease rentals USD (~$1.2B/yr); spares imports; revenue INR
Fare hikes reduce discretionary travel; load factor pressure
International routes ~30% revenue; weaker INR helps

dimensions.explanation: Load factor down 2-3pp; yield up 8-10%; net RASK flat to slightly up
dimensions.evidence: Historical: fare hikes ~60-70% cost pass-through; volume elasticity -0.8

dimensions.explanation: Fare hikes implemented quickly; market leader pricing power; but ceiling exists
dimensions.evidence: IndiGo leads fare increases; competitors follow

dimensions.explanation: ATF cost up 25-30%; no hedging; lease rentals up on weaker INR
EBITDA margin compression 800-1000bps; CASK-RASK gap widens
Advance bookings (cash positive); but fuel payables increase
dimensions.evidence: Negative WC cycle normally; fuel credit 15-30 days

dimensions.explanation: High lease liabilities (Ind AS 116); USD debt service burden up
Net USD payables (leases, spares, intl airport charges); no natural hedge
Spares lead time up; engine shop visits costly; Airbus/Pratt delivery delays
Price-sensitive leisure travel hit; corporate resilient; VFR stable
UDAN, slot rules stable; no policy change
Operational excellence maintained; on-time performance leader

Promoter (Gangwal) vs management governance settled; board stable
